   - Incorporate dry-land exercises like pull-ups, push-ups, and resistance band drills to build the specific muscles used in open-water technique.

   - Practice open-water-specific drills (e.g., 100s with a "stay upright" focus) to train good posture and visibility in crowded or choppy conditions.

   - Learn to swim efficiently in a group, which mimics race conditions. Stay in the slipstream of other swimmers with minimal effort.

   - Simulate low-visibility scenarios by swimming at night or wearing a blindfold. This builds confidence and awareness in challenging conditions.

   - Swim at a slightly higher stroke rate (e.g., 60–70 strokes per minute) to help you stay on the surface and conserve energy during long distances.

   - Work on your open-water dive technique. Focus on looking up early in the stroke to maintain better balance and reduce splash at the surface.
